archetypes.name: Divide Polynomials by Long Division
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.4 — Dividing Polynomials
archetypes.coreConcept: Polynomial long division repeatedly cancels the current leading term, then subtracts and brings down the next term until the remainder has lower degree than the divisor.
archetypes.mentalModel: Each quotient term removes one leading-term mismatch; writing every degree column keeps like terms aligned and subtraction must act on the entire product row.
archetypes.governingRelation: dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder; degree(remainder) < degree(divisor) or remainder = 0

cognitiveTraps.description: Failing to distribute subtraction to every term in the product row.
Leaving out a missing degree column so later coefficients shift into the wrong powers.
Stopping while the residual polynomial still has degree at least that of the divisor.

archetypes.figureNone: The skill is symbolic polynomial manipulation; a figure would not clarify the coefficient alignment or subtraction.

archetypes.name: Check a Quotient and Remainder
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.4 — Dividing Polynomials
archetypes.coreConcept: The quotient and remainder are correct exactly when multiplying the divisor by the quotient and adding the remainder reconstructs the dividend, with a remainder degree below the divisor's degree.
archetypes.mentalModel: Treat division as a reversible decomposition: multiply back, add the remainder, and verify both the identity and the remainder-degree condition.

cognitiveTraps.description: Checking divisor times quotient but omitting the nonzero remainder.
Accepting a remainder whose degree is not lower than the divisor's degree.

archetypes.figureNone: The division identity and degree condition are checked algebraically without a meaningful visual representation.

archetypes.name: Use Synthetic Division for x−k
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.4 — Dividing Polynomials
archetypes.coreConcept: Synthetic division is a compact coefficient-only form for dividing by a monic linear divisor x−k; the final entry is the remainder.
archetypes.mentalModel: The divisor determines k with its sign reversed from the constant term; bring down the leading coefficient, then alternate multiplying by k and adding.
archetypes.governingRelation: divisor=x-k; synthetic input=k; bottom-row coefficients form q(x), final entry r

cognitiveTraps.description: Using the constant in x−k directly instead of its opposite as the synthetic input k.
Omitting a zero coefficient for an absent power and shifting the remaining entries.
Treating the final synthetic-division entry as another quotient coefficient instead of the remainder.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: last entry -> coefficient of x^0 in q

archetypes.figureNone: Synthetic division is a coefficient algorithm; a diagram would not improve understanding beyond the aligned computation.

archetypes.name: Reconstruct a Dividend from Division Data
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.4 — Dividing Polynomials
archetypes.coreConcept: Given a divisor, quotient, and remainder, the original dividend is recovered by multiplying the first two and adding the remainder.
archetypes.mentalModel: Reverse the division algorithm one operation at a time, preserving every term of the remainder and checking the resulting degree.

cognitiveTraps.description: Subtracting the remainder when reconstructing the dividend instead of adding it.
Multiplying only the leading terms of divisor and quotient and omitting cross terms.
Reconstructing the dividend from divisor and quotient but omitting the stated remainder.

archetypes.figureNone: The inverse calculation is an exact symbolic identity, so a figure would not add information.
